findings.title: Single-color gray ink is silently discarded
findings.why_it_matters: A supported DOCX image containing crisp gray or colored text on white can publish with an empty OCR page even though its text is visible. When every foreground pixel has the same nonzero grayscale value, the background-excluding histogram has one occupied bin, every variance is zero, and argmax selects threshold zero; printed_ink therefore becomes false and the printed recognizer is skipped. Handling the singleton histogram explicitly preserves these pixels while retaining the existing threshold behavior for ordinary multilevel scans.
findings.suggested_fix: Before calculating the variance, detect a histogram with exactly one occupied bin and return the gray<245 foreground mask (equivalently threshold at that occupied bin). Keep the existing all-white case. Verify a white-background embedded DOCX PNG whose text pixels all have grayscale value 128 reaches recognition and publishes its text rather than an empty page.
evidence: For white plus gray-128 input, the sole histogram bin is 128: below it weight=moment=0, and at/above it weight=H and moment=128H. Every numerator is zero, argmax is 0, and the returned mask contains no pixels.

backend/app/document_worker.py:226-237 -- DOCX image bytes are converted to RGB, passed to prepare_image(...,'complete'), then recognized and staged; lines 242-245 publish a successful revision without requiring nonempty page text.

findings.title: Complete OCR interleaves printed columns
findings.why_it_matters: A two-column printed page processed in complete mode loses Paddle's reading order, even when there is no handwriting. For returned lines ordered left-top, left-bottom, right-top, right-bottom, the new y/x sort publishes left-top, right-top, left-bottom, right-bottom, mixing the text of separate columns in the document view and source spans. Retaining the recognizer's printed sequence and inserting handwriting within its column avoids changing correct printed page order.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the unconditional global y/x sort from finish_page. Preserve the printed lines' returned sequence; insert transcribed handwriting into the corresponding overlapping column using the geometry-based insertion already used by compose_page for skip blocks. At minimum, purely printed complete pages must retain their recognizer order. Verify both a two-column printed page and a mixed page whose handwritten insertion must not reorder the remaining printed lines.
evidence: backend/app/ocr.py:285-291 -- The sort is inside mode=='complete' but outside the handwriting loop, so it executes for complete pages with an empty handwriting list.
backend/app/ocr.py:67 --     # Keep the recognizer's printed reading order and insert omissions in their column.
backend/app/ocr.py:76-81 -- compose_page builds the stored text and span offsets in the incoming blocks' order.

backend/app/document_worker.py:211-216,227-237 -- Actual PDF and embedded DOCX OCR results flow from finish_page into stage_page and document publication; embedded DOCX images explicitly use complete mode.
